open_errors.issue: Devan says he has watched Muthu write grey-wax letters 'for a year'. Everywhere else he has seen them for six years: ch 8 counts six years of letters, ch 19 says Muthu 'had written to Kodiyur every month for six years', and ch 24 says 'For six years I let you carry grey letters'.
open_errors.fix: Change 'for a year' to 'for six years'.

patches.find: I've watched him write grey-wax letters for a year.
patches.replace: I've watched him write grey-wax letters for six years.

open_errors.issue: Neela says Janu told her about Devan's eight years without sparring 'in the second week'. In book 1 Janu told her this in ch 3, the day after the wedding, which is the first week (F047).

patches.find: Janu told me in the second week. Eight years.
patches.replace: Janu told me in the first week. Eight years.

open_errors.issue: The narration says the words of the tappers' song 'had never come, not past the first verses'. Neela heard Ammu sing the last verse ('the name given back') in book 1 ch 20, and she recalls that line in ch 27 of this book. Read literally, the ch 7 line says she does not know it.
open_errors.fix: Make it clear she knows the last verse from Ammu.

patches.find: The words had never come, not past the first verses.
patches.replace: The words had never come back to her whole, only the first verses and the last, which Ammu had sung her once.

open_errors.issue: The five Kettamala men outside the Resin House wall are described in 'Kettamala brown'. Every other description of the garrison has them in grey (ch 28 'Garrison grey', ch 29 and ch 30 'in their grey').

patches.find: five men in Kettamala brown huddled round a cold fire
patches.replace: five men in Kettamala grey huddled round a cold fire

open_errors.issue: The narration says Devan 'had never seen that face by day'. In ch 7 he watched Vellan cross the Resin House yard in daylight from the ridge and said 'That's him'.
open_errors.fix: Allow for the earlier sighting, which was distant.

patches.find: He had never seen that face by day, and he knew it, the way you know a stair in the dark.
patches.replace: He had seen that face by day only once, from a ridge, too far to read, and he knew it, the way you know a stair in the dark.

open_errors.issue: Vellan says the night-guard's wrist scars are 'there, same as yours'. In ch 2, First Guard's wrist shows a single smooth, flat seam, explicitly 'nothing like' Neela's layered ridges, and Neela repeats this in ch 32. Vellan explains the bare throat (paste) but not the smooth seam, so the clue does not resolve under the scar rule (F014).
open_errors.fix: Have Vellan explain why the wrist ridges show as a smooth seam.

patches.find: The wrists they hide in cuffs. The scars are there, same as yours.
patches.replace: The wrists they hide in cuffs, and a palace surgeon pares the old ridges smooth, so a slipped cuff shows one seam. The scars are there under it, same as yours.
